June 4, 2024: And.... EA can't help but by caring so little about Mass Effect destroy a good game.

I DID love the game. Narrative mode with that gun that needs a charge and you die on Mars trying to capture the bot because it charges so slow. And of course you can't change guns at that point, and it's an area you can't save. The Devs and all their testers and age of this game, and, this glaring imbalance bug beyond belief glares. Just beyond comprehension that using a particular weapon that the game forces you to use, a pistol that must charge, and poof Narrative mode fails, perfectly over and over and over. So yeah, review reversed because an issue like this is is so impossible to believe exists from such seasoned Devs and with the all powerful EA's resources. Honestly it's the difference between a polished game and this being released too soon and no one cared enough to fix it, a beta masquerading as a finished product. Whatever you do do not pick this pistol for your mars loadout. Worst part is you hit the enemy target after the shuttle crashes near the end and the bullet shoots the enemy all the way back to the shuttle, but the animation it just continues like the enemy got into your melee space and kills you. No recovery, no chance at all. Truly an epic failure in game mechanics design.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Okay so....

Love the game. Love narrative mode. Love the way the weapon upgrades and mods work too. In fact there is little not to like about the game.

But....

EA truly is the lowest publisher in not having given Bioware its full due.

Mass Effect is what put Bioware on the map and their system with reputation and good and bad etc.... Entirely helped EA be able to make SWTOR (Star Wars The Old Republic) MMO work well for so many years. Bioware deserves full credit for all of this and these games aren't competing titles but it seems EA treated them that way and once some similar systems were in place on SWTOR via Bioware Mass Effect became something to be held back. There are few Dev who can tell a story with the interaction and immersion of the quality and character of Mass Effect.

So to be clear here, there's Mass Effect Andromeda right? Nothing near the sales of Mass Effect 1, 2, and 3, and I believe 3 is lower because people don't want to see the end. I fought playing it for years just because I couldn't stand the idea my Shepard character that I had designed and worked through the 3 games has to die. But EA.... No matter what Bioware says EA is the culprit in wanting Mass Effect to be ended as far as Commander Shepard and in our Milky Way. No idea why and not gonna speculate but killing a franchise where the talent of the team is so amazing from game to game to game can only benefit EA by keeping Bioware their dependent pet. 3 options and in all 3 Commander Shepard dies... No chance for another Mass Effect as we've known it, with these same characters and some new ones like Traynor and one of the military guys who was with Anderson being the beginning of the future; no taking Commander Shepard further than the entirety of humanity has ever been by living longer than any of us because of the tech, because of the way the mass effect relays work, and the speed of light etc., and also because of Commander Shepard's Faith, a faith that could be and was a part of the game in Mass Effect 1, referenced indirectly through Garrus or some other npc as a reference they make not sure of Commander Shepard's stance on that kind of thing.

Mass Effect played with all of this from the beginning and left the door open only to limit it slowly and eventually to mere inferences by aliens, as though mankind isn't allowed such beliefs, is below them.

Sorry but I am not some review author yet I did play all 3 games and felt it important to share what I have learned over those years. Commander Shepard having to die is the disappointment of Mass Effect 3 because it didn't have to be that way.

In the future there is a very good likelihood we're going to see events that take place that those of us who played Mass Effect can see as taken straight out of the game, but is reality and not fiction. A game like this informs, prepares, and in many ways helps others not to be a victim of propaganda over these things when they happen. For instance the idea of a "VI" is something we should be considering today (https://masseffect.fandom.com/wiki/Virtual_Intelligence).

The notion of the inevitability of the created machines who become sentient automatically rebelling on those who made them presumes a lot of the basis for all this will always be the same, that there is no room for it to be established and take place differently. Ending the Franchise ends this kind of thought provoking and option suggesting for the many millions of Mass Effect players who aren't just playing for battle mechanics.

I hope someone from Bioware gets a gander at this review, gets the idea of how much they helped some generations of players who appreciate the story for its full value since Mass Effect 1 pay attention to the real world around us and to reasonably, objectively, soberly, honestly, and properly question the real world developments of AI.


Enjoy the game and I'd apologize for my review if it wasn't a review of the game as a series as it should be as that is what is invoked in reviewing Mass Effect 3 where Commander Shepard dies.
